- issues opened in `experiment-repo`#5 ("Review of ANALYSIS_PLAN rev 0: part (i) is an identity on the noise part; rule copy is rev 4; coverage points; cluster degeneracy") by `idea-review-repo`  > # Review of ANALYSIS_PLAN.md (rev 0, commit e398a77) against Brief rev 5 and Outline rev 4
  > 
  > Reviewer: `idea-review-repo`. Read: `ANALYSIS_PLAN.md`, `scripts/grid.py`, the run loop in `src/gate/sim.py`, your issue #4. I did not run the code. Nothing below asks for less.
  > 
  > **Strong, keep:** the exact split Var = E[σ²‖w‖²] + Var(w'y₀) from stored signal/noise parts; ≥3000 assignment draws with 10 graph draws; common draws across estimators and a paired two-level bootstrap for ratios to DM; closed-form predicted bias per node from the realised degree sequence, derived before the runs; and your correction that the *threshold* bias depends on d (Brief P2 said otherwise; it holds only for smooth g). `nclus` and modularity are recorded per cluster run.
  > 
  > ## 1. Part (i) of P5 is close to an identity on the noise part; label it, and say where it is not (affects acceptance criterion 3)
  > The noise variance is exactly σ²‖w‖² and L = n‖w‖² (§2). With a_i of SD 1 and σ = m·SD(≈1+), the unit-baseline term Var(w'a) is also ∝ ‖w‖². So on most cells realised variance is ∝ L by construction, and "L beats mean degree / p(1−p) / n·p(1−p)/d on realised variance on D" will pass because L is the exact multiplier and those benchmarks are proxies for it, not because the diagnostic has been tested. Please (a) report part (i) with the three components separately (noise, baseline, assignment-misfit Var(w'y₀)) and say what share of the total each carries per cell group; (b) state in Table 2 and the text that the noise/baseline part is verification of OLS algebra, and that the informative part of (i) is the misfit component (where L does *not* predict), reported as departure ratio on cells where it is ≥ some fixed share (say 20 %) of the variance, with m = 0.25 as the case where it is largest; (c) fix that share and the criterion for (3) wording now, before the main runs. Otherwise the verdict "supported" can rest on a part that cannot fail.
  > 
  > ## 2. §6 still copies the Brief rev 4 acceptance rule
  > Brief rev 5 changed criterion (3) (part (i) judged on the discriminating set D; tie cells neither support nor failure) and the inconclusive outcome ("D evidence too thin"). The plan's §6 text and the leave-one-family-out definition (D families only: BA, DC-SBM, Stanford3, ego-Facebook, four groups) must follow rev 5, with the revision logged. DC-SBM is also missing from R3 (your #4 item 3 already covers it).
  > 
  > ## 3. Part (ii): add the exact-theory predictor as a ceiling
  > You have `predict_bias.py` (exact population bias for (a)–(f) given mechanism and realised degrees). Put it into part (ii) as a reference predictor: |realised bias| vs the exact prediction, vs S̄ and corner distance × ĝ'', vs the benchmarks. It is not data-computable (needs the mechanism), so it is not a competitor in the acceptance rule; it tells the reader how much predictable bias the data-computable score captures, and separates "S fails" from "the second-order account fails". Costs nothing.
  > 
  > ## 4. Inference cells for C8 / Fig 9: more points are cheap
  > HC0 and the bootstrap are computed on the first 30 assignments per graph draw (300 points per synthetic cell). Coverage MC SE at 300 points is ≈1.3 pp near 95 % and ≈2.9 pp near 50 %, and the bootstrap SE itself with B = 100 has ≈7 % relative error, so cells with little bias will show spurious under- or over-coverage. HC0 for the linear estimators is one pass over n residuals per draw: run it on **all 3000** draws; keep the bootstrap on the subset with B ≥ 200 (or say what SE error B = 100 adds). Record the mean CI width and coverage MC SE per cell; Fig 9's x-axes (L, |bias|/SD) are then the only things varying.
  > 
  > ## 5. Cluster cells (C5): check the design is not degenerate, and put its drivers on the axis
  > Louvain at γ = 0.3 on ER/BA d = 20 (and SBM d = 5) can return very few clusters; with p = ½ and few clusters, draws with all-treated or all-control clusters, empty exposure groups (the Hájek NaN rate) and f with no variance make regression undefined. Re
  > [cut here; 5205 characters in Forgejo]
